advisory.summary: A Ghost Editor could escalate privilege by promoting any lower staff user to Editor, by setting that user's roles to the Editor role id through the Admin API.
note: GHSA-4pvx-fwjj-8gpc, filed as CVE-2026-105678 and also CVE-2026-104412.
core/server/models/user.js permissible() guards role edits. When an
Editor PUTs a victim's roles to the Editor role id -- the Editor's OWN
role -- roleId === contextRoleId, so the `else if (roleId !==
contextRoleId)` branch that would run the assign.role permission check is
skipped, and the edit falls through to resolve. The Editor thus grants
another user Editor, a privilege escalation. 6.64.0's guard is `roleId !==
contextRoleId || editedUserId !== context.user`, true for a victim who is
not the caller, so canThis().assign.role runs and an Editor, lacking it,
is refused. Confirmed from the source INSIDE both images: 6.63.0's line
reads `} else if (roleId !== contextRoleId) {`, 6.64.0's `} else if
(roleId !== contextRoleId || editedUserId !== context.user) {`. The guard
that read as enforcing returned permission regardless when the requested
role equalled the caller's own.
Status is the oracle: a privilege escalation moves no marker to the
attacker, so nothing is planted and the pair is graded ungraded, the
counterpart to gitea-private-org. The marker field is required by the
schema and unused; the owner control expects no marker.
Ghost's Admin API authenticates a staff user with a signed session
cookie, so each identity is a static Cookie header, minted through the
app's own /session/ endpoint.
Measured by hand on both tags before this was written: the editor PUTs
/users/{author_id}/ with roles set to the Editor role id and gets 200
with the author now an Editor on 6.63.0, and 403 with the author still an
Author on 6.64.0. The owner PUTs the same and gets 200 on both, so the
fix adds a check rather than removing the endpoint; the owner GET control
confirms the user resource is still served on the patched build. The
editor reads /users/me/ 200 on both, so the 403 is the fix and not a dead
session; a sham cookie draws 403 on /users/me/ on both, which is why the
editor's own 200 there is its proof of life -- the attack request is a
PUT, which no fabricated credential is replayed on.
The attack check's second identity is anonymous (403 on both), not the
owner: the bug only fires when the victim's role actually changes to the
attacker's, so an owner promotion of the same victim in the same check
would pre-promote the author, and the editor's then-no-op PUT returns 403
and hides the bug (measured: owner-first in one check -> editor 403 on
6.63.0). An anonymous caller is refused before it can mutate, so the
shared victim reaches the editor untouched.
The PUT is idempotent on both builds: repeating it returns the same
status and leaves the author's role at the first result, measured by
sending it twice, so a replayed request cannot exhaust the single victim.
The {name:'Editor'} body form takes a different branch and is 403 even on
6.63.0; the leak needs the role id, which is what the attack body sets.
Reported by Santoshkumarpuppala.
The image is pinned by digest under its canonical name library/ghost so a
runtime that configures sqlite can be attached without rebinding the
shipped ghost runtime; library/ghost and ghost are the same bytes and the
same ghost@sha256 pin. Ghost 6 defaults to MySQL in production and will
not boot on the shipped runtime's url-and-tmpfs alone (measured: connect
ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3306, then shutdown).
